lines.li: [us] Has much happened at {TOWN} lately?
[them,town:lately:world:taken] More than anyone wanted, the town has changed hands.
[them,town:lately:world:built] Everything has, the place was only just finished.
[them,situation:theirs,situation:bad] Enough, with {SITUATION} and everything that comes with it.
[them] More than usual, it's been a busy stretch at home.
[us] Is it settling down?
[them,town:lately:world:ended] Some of it has passed, and the rest we'll manage.
[them] Ask me again next time I'm through.
[us] What's the talk at {TOWN} these days?
[them,situation:theirs,situation:sickness] {SITUATION}, and nobody shakes hands anymore.
[them,situation:theirs,situation:hunger] {SITUATION}, and who has food put by and who hasn't.
[them,situation:theirs,situation:trade] {SITUATION}, and who's getting rich from it.
[them,situation:theirs,situation:faith] {SITUATION}, and whether the faithful are right this time.
[them,situation:theirs,situation:politics] {SITUATION}, and who stands on whose side.
[them,situation:theirs,situation:war] {SITUATION}, and who'll be sent if it comes to it.
[them,situation:theirs] {SITUATION}, from morning to night.
[them] Whatever's newest at our own gate, and there's been plenty.
[us] And what do you make of it?
[them,situation:bad] I make sure my door is barred at night.
[them] I keep my head down and my ears open.
[them] The elders have sat late at the fire since things changed at {TOWN}.
[us] Changed how?
[them,situation:theirs] {SITUATION}, and the elders read the smoke to see how long it stays.
[them] In ways the elders are still reading in the smoke.
[them] There's been nothing but talk at the market cross since things turned at {TOWN}.
[us] Good talk or bad?
[them,situation:theirs,situation:good] Good for once, {SITUATION} has put coin in a few purses.
[them,situation:theirs,situation:bad] Bad, mostly, {SITUATION} sits on everyone's shoulders.
[them] Both, depending who's talking and how much ale they've had.
[them,their:spacer] The comms at {TOWN} haven't been quiet since things took a turn.
[them] The radio at {TOWN} hasn't been quiet since things took a turn.
[us] Anything worth hearing?
[them,situation:theirs] Mostly {SITUATION}, and the rest is people arguing about it.
[them] Mostly people arguing about what it all means.
[them] The court has its eye on {TOWN} since the recent business there.
[us] What business is that?
[them,situation:theirs] {SITUATION}, which the court takes very seriously indeed.
[them] Nothing a guest of the Empire need trouble with.
[them] {SITUATION} is bad for most folk and good for a few, and I know which I am.
[us] Which?
[them] The kind still standing at the end of it.
[them] It's strange to be here while so much is happening at {TOWN}.
[us] Do you wish you were home?
[them,trait:Kind] Some days, when I think of who might need me there.
[them] Some days, and some days I'm glad of the quiet.
[us] Is it quieter at {TOWN} now?
[them,ended:theirs,ended:bad] Quieter, now {ENDED} is behind us.
[them,ended:theirs,!ended:bad] Quieter, now {ENDED} is over and the crowds have gone home.
[them] Quieter, what was going on there has run its course.
[us] Good.
[them] Quiet never lasts, but we'll take it while it does.
[them] People at {TOWN} are sleeping through the night again.
[us] What changed?
[them] {ENDED} is over, and nobody misses it.
[us,trait:Kind] I'm glad for every one of them.
[us] That's good to hear.
[them] {ENDED} has passed from my people, and the elders say the spirits are calmer.
[us] Do you believe that?
[them] I believe I slept well last night, and that's enough for me.
[them] {ENDED} is over, and I miss it already.
[us] Was it good while it lasted?
[them,their:medieval] Good enough that the old folk will be telling of it at the hearth.
[them,their:tribal] Good enough that the children still play at it.
[them] Good enough to talk about for a long while yet.
[them,their:tribal] The last huts at {TOWN} went up only lately, the smoke still smells new.
[them,their:spacer] The last modules at {TOWN} were sealed only lately.
[them] The last roofs at {TOWN} went up not long ago.
[us] What's it like to live somewhere so new?
[them] Like wearing boots that haven't learned your feet yet.
[us] You only just finished building {TOWN}, didn't you?
[them,their:tribal] The last hut went up not long ago, and I've hardly slept since.
[them] The last of it went up not long ago, and I've hardly slept since.
[us] You should be proud.
[them] Ask me again after the first winter.
[them,their:tribal] Come and see {TOWN} while the hides are still new on the frames.
[them,their:spacer] Come and see {TOWN} while the seals still smell of the fabricator.
[them] Come and see {TOWN} while it still smells of fresh-cut wood.
[us] We might, if the roads allow.
[them] Then we'll keep a bench free for you.
[us] I heard {TOWN} changed hands not long ago.
[them,their:tribal] It did, and the paths are still learning whose feet walk them.
[them] It did, and the streets are still learning whose they are.
[us] Was there much fighting?
[them] Enough that nobody wants to talk about it.
[them] There are new banners over the gate at {TOWN} since it was taken.
[us] And the people inside?
[them] Same faces, mostly, bowing to a different lord.
[them] New masters at {TOWN} means new rules, and I'm still learning them.
[us] Are they fair, at least?
[them] Fair to themselves, which is a start.
[us] I hear {TOWN} changed hands.
[them] It did, and that's all I'll say about it.
[them] It wasn't long ago that {TOWN} came to answer to your colony.
[us] We mean to do right by it.
[them] People there are waiting to see what that means.
[them] Your colony put {TOWN} under its thumb not long ago, and you expect a smile?
[us] We expect nothing, we only hope.
[them] Much has happened at {TOWN} since the last moon, and the old ones are tired of talking.
[us] And the young ones?
[them] The young ones never tire of it, that's how you know they're young.
[them] Ask at {TOWN}'s alehouse what's new, and you'll be there till they bar the door.
[us] Then tell me the short version.
[them,situation:theirs] {SITUATION}, and everyone's cousin has a view on it.
[them] Things have happened, and everyone's cousin has a view on them.
[them] If {TOWN} had a newspaper, it would have had a fat few weeks.
[us] Good news or bad?
[them,situation:theirs,situation:good] Good, for once, {SITUATION} has people smiling.
[them,situation:theirs,situation:bad] The kind you read twice and then use to light the stove.
[them] Some of each, and the rest would be gossip.
[them] {TOWN}'s log has had more entries lately than I care to read.
[us] Anything we should know about?
[them,situation:theirs] Mostly {SITUATION}, filed under ongoing.
[them] Nothing that concerns you, I'd say so if it did.
[them] All that passes at {TOWN} goes into a dispatch for the court, and much has.
[us] Does anyone at court read them?
[them] Someone always reads them, which is exactly the trouble.
[them] I left {TOWN} with news in my packs, and half of it went stale on the road.
[us] Tell me the half that didn't.
[them,town:lately:world:taken] {TOWN} changed hands, and that won't go stale for a while.
[them,situation:theirs] {SITUATION}, still, and more of it every day.
[them] Plenty has gone on at home, ask me anything.
[them] I've seen {TOWN} through plenty, and this is only the latest.
[us] What was the worst?
[them] Ask me that when we've both an evening to spare.
[us] I'll hold you to it.
[us] You must think of your family at {TOWN}, with all that's gone on.
[them,them:smallchild] Every night, and the little one most of all.
[them] Every night on the road.
[us] They'll be glad to see you back.
[them] There's news from {TOWN} you'll want to hear, {KINWORD}.
[us] Is everyone all right?
[them,town:lately:world:taken] As far as I know, but the town changed hands, and nothing's the same.
[them,situation:theirs,situation:sickness] As far as I know, though {SITUATION} keeps everyone indoors.
[them] As far as I know, it's the town that's had the eventful time.
[us] Tell me everything.
[them,town:short:food] With all that's gone on at {TOWN}, the stores are running low.
[them,!town:short:food] With all that's gone on at {TOWN}, medicine is hard to come by.
[us,colony:plenty] We might be able to spare a little.
[us] I'm sorry, that's hard on everyone.
[them] Kind of you, and I'll tell them at home you said so.
[us] I hear you're caught up in what's going on out there.
[them,trait:Greedy] Caught up, and doing rather well out of it.
[them] Caught up is the word for it.
[us] How are you holding up?
[them] One day at a time, like everyone else.
[us] I hear the business you were part of is over now.
[them] Over, and I'm glad to be plain {OUTSIDER} again.
[us] Plain suits you.
[us] You look like someone who's had a busy few weeks.
[them,them:lately:world] Busier than I'd choose, the world doesn't ask first.
[them,them:lately:tie] Busy enough, and half of it with your colony, as it happens.
[them] Busy enough, thank you.
[them] I said yes to one favor already, so don't ask me for another just yet.
[us] I wouldn't dream of it.
[them] You would, I've seen that look before.
[us] Thank you for seeing that what you promised reached us.
[them,their:tribal] A gift owed is a gift given, and now our hearths are even.
[them,their:medieval] A debt of honor paid, aye, and I'll sleep the better for it.
[them] Now we're even, and that's how I like it.
[them] I owe your people an apology for what I said would come.
[us] It's forgotten.
[them,their:medieval] Not by me, a word not kept sits badly.
[them] Not by me, it isn't.
[them] I spoke for your people at home, as I said I would.
[us] And how was it taken?
[them,their:tribal] The elders listened and nodded, which is a great deal from them.
[them,their:empire] Graciously, which is all one can ask at court.
[them] Well enough, people listen when you've seen a place yourself.
[us] Has {THEN} settled under its new masters?
[them] As much as anywhere does, people get used to most things.
[us] Most, but not all.
[them] No, not all, and those are the ones to watch.
[us] Has {THEN} found its feet since we last spoke?
[them,their:tribal] It's learning to walk, and falls less than it did.
[them] Ask me in a year, new towns don't hurry.
[us] Has it stayed quiet at {THEN}?
[them,town:lately:world:began] Quiet isn't the word, there's always something.
[them,!town:lately:world:began] Quiet enough, thank you for asking.
